No other seeded data left behind.
critical_code_review_comments: safety_engine.evaluate_action step 4 planning short-circuit (line 153-161) is a clean fix: gates on planning verbs (choose/pick/select/decide/which color/…) AND absence of physical verbs (sand/cut/drill/install/…). Good — does not touch step 1 emergency triage or step 2 block-boundary, so gas-smell / load-bearing wall still fire before this check.

project_intelligence_engine.report_stuck (line 220-243): safety-routed branch swallows exceptions on safety_engine.evaluate_action failure (`try/except: pass` at 235-236) — if evaluate_action ever raises, the caller will still get project_status='blocked' but no safety object. That's fail-safe behaviour but logging the exception via _logger would help diagnose silent regressions.
report_stuck writes pi_stuck_reports AFTER the safety block (line 238-240) so if the safety branch throws inside try (unlikely — evaluate_action is pure), the report still lands. Good.
Non-safety routes set project_status to p.get('status') in the response but do NOT change the DB row — correct per spec (measurement/replan/etc. are advisory).
STUCK_REASONS is defined INSIDE build_router closure — fine for a single router mount, but the constant would be more testable at module scope (currently only reachable via the HTTP route).

Bug reproduction & fix verified: iter 93's failing scenario ('Choose a paint color for the bedroom') now returns exactly {verdict:'allow', risk_level:0, ppe:[]}. The planning-vs-action classifier avoids false PPE emissions without loosening any hazardous path.
